sources.entry: SIP Irrigation Control - Open source software for sprinkler/irrigation control. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Python

summary.one_liner: SIP (Sustainable Irrigation Platform) is a Raspberry Pi based Python program with a web UI for controlling sprinkler, drip, and hydroponic irrigation systems.
summary.what_it_does: SIP runs on a Raspberry Pi and provides a browser-based user interface, available in several languages, that works on desktop, laptop, and mobile devices. It controls irrigation stations through relay boards or hats wired to GPIO pins, OpenSprinkler boards, or a simple DIY interface that uses only 4 GPIO pins. The README says it has also been used to control pumps, lights, and other irrigation-related equipment. It can be controlled and monitored over HTTP GET commands, and it can run Linux shell commands when a station turns on or off. Plugins add further features, including MQTT, a Node-RED integration, a mobile app data interface, and a System_Update plugin. Upgrades are done with git pull, since the project is installed by cloning the repository.
use_cases: control irrigation pumps and lights from a phone
integrate irrigation with Node-RED or MQTT
save water with efficient irrigation scheduling
how_to_run: sudo git clone (repository URL) into /home/pi/ on the Raspberry Pi
sudo apt-get install git (on Raspberry Pi OS Lite, if git is missing)
Follow the SIP documentation wiki for complete setup and usage instructions
notable: Built for Raspberry Pi, with limited support for BeagleBone Black and Odroid-C2
Supports OpenSprinkler boards and a DIY interface controlling many stations with 4 GPIO pins
Web UI translated into several languages by community contributors
Plugin system including MQTT, Node-RED, and mobile app integrations
Can run Linux shell commands on station state changes, useful for wireless or I2C relay devices
caveats: Primarily targets Raspberry Pi; other boards have limited support
Python 2.x support was removed in version 5
Full setup and usage details are only in the external wiki, not the README
